tldr: This is a theme thread of mostly arXiv papers, not one developing story. Since Nov 4 it has tracked RL for agents: multi-turn and multi-agent training, RL-learned memory, rollout cost, and the finding that RL tool-use gains can raise tool hallucination.
whats_new: Nov 23: CO-GRAFT finds query generation explains at most 15% of RL gains in Search-R1 agents, and a state-verified RL paper lifts a 27B tutoring agent from 51.47% to 80.74% strict success.
why_it_matters: If you post-train or operate tool-using agents, this cluster names where RL pays off and what it costs: rollout throughput, tool hallucination, and which agent role actually improved, though nearly every result is author-reported.

beats.headline: RL methods aim at multi-turn and multi-agent systems
beats.summary: A study of what multi-turn RL improves, AutoRL running the training pipeline, imitation-bootstrapped MARL, and SLICR's logic-shaped rewards.

beats.headline: RL is used to learn what to keep in bounded memory
beats.summary: Test-time model-based RL for world-model memory and MaxIM incremental summaries.

beats.headline: Rollout cost gets attacked from sampler, scheduler and GPU placement
beats.summary: FewStepRL, the ASP rollout scheduler, vLLM's 107x TPU v7 cycle speedup, CTRL's learner/rollout co-residency, and latent world-model rollouts for VLA policies.

beats.headline: Better task scores can mean more tool hallucination, so papers add state-awareness, scaffolds and stop rules
beats.summary: AutoScaffold, StateAlign, Learn then Bet intervention rules, and safe in-context RL under a cost budget.

beats.headline: Applied RL papers ride along on shared vocabulary
beats.summary: ReShap interpretability for multi-action policies and RLDE iterative document editing.

beats.headline: Continual RL: learning new tasks without losing old ones
beats.summary: Policy-improvement-guided replay and grid cells as spectral successor features.

beats.headline: Where RL gains come from in tool-using agents: verified state, data reweighting, role attribution
beats.summary: AOVO drops tool-specific rewards, state-verified RL trains tutoring agents against a deterministic checker, and CO-GRAFT splits Search-R1 gains by role.

open_questions: Does StateAlign's reduction in tool hallucination hold on tool APIs outside the paper's own benchmarks?
Does vLLM's 107x RL cycle speedup on TPU v7 carry over to policies larger than Qwen3-0.6B?
Does CTRL's 1.11-2.24x throughput over verl's async baselines show up in an independent reproduction?
Do learned intervention rules like Learn then Bet beat turn limits on production agent runs without stopping good runs early?
If query generation explains at most 15% of Search-R1's RL gain, which role carries the rest, and does the split hold for other search agents?
Does state-verified RL transfer beyond tutoring workspaces to agents whose state has no deterministic verifier?
take_for_builders: When evaluating an RL-tuned agent, score tool-hallucination rate and per-role behavior (query, read, answer) next to task success, since the headline gain can hide regressions or come from one role.
